drills.q: What backbone did DiT replace, and what was the key scaling claim?
drills.a: Replaced the U-Net with a ViT-style transformer on patchified latent tokens; FID scales predictably with transformer Gflops, mirroring LLM scaling laws.

drills.q: Why is the AdaLN-Zero gate initialized to zero?
drills.a: So every DiT block starts training as an identity function, giving stable training from step one without careful warmup.

drills.q: What are spacetime patches, and why does doubling video duration roughly quadruple attention cost?
drills.a: Spacetime patches are tokens extracted from a spatially-and-temporally compressed video latent. Attention is quadratic in total token count, which scales with frames x spatial patches, so doubling duration alone roughly doubles tokens and quadruples attention cost.

drills.q: How does flow matching's training objective differ from diffusion's score prediction?
drills.a: Flow matching regresses a velocity field along an explicitly chosen probability path (e.g. a straight line) via simulation-free L2 loss, instead of predicting the score of an implicit reverse-time SDE.

drills.q: Why does a rectified (straight-line) flow path allow fewer sampling steps than a typical diffusion path?
drills.a: The straight path has low curvature and a constant target velocity, so a coarse integrator (even one Euler step in the limit) tracks it accurately, unlike a curved path which needs many small steps to avoid discretization error.

drills.q: Why did SD3.5, FLUX, Veo, and Movie Gen all adopt flow matching by 2024-25?
drills.a: Fewer required sampling steps translate directly into serving cost/latency cuts at scale -- roughly a 10x reduction in steps is most of the unit-economics case for serving millions of generations a day.

drills.q: How does a consistency model differ from simply truncating a diffusion model's sampling steps?
drills.a: A consistency model is explicitly trained so any point on a trajectory maps to the same clean output, enabling accurate 1-4 step generation. Truncating an ordinary diffusion/flow model's steps produces a blurry, degraded sample since it was never trained for that coarse a step size.

drills.q: Give the LCM distillation cost/speed/quality numbers for a 768x768 2-4 step model.
drills.a: ~32 A100-GPU-hours to distill from a pretrained SD checkpoint, 10-100x inference speedup, matches 25-50-step DDIM on FID/alignment at 2-4 steps, with quality degrading sharply as step count approaches 1.

drills.q: What does VBench2's physics-and-commonsense dimension reveal about the state of video generation in 2026?
drills.a: Every current model, including frontier ones like Veo 3, still shows a real measured gap between visual plausibility and actual physical consistency.

drills.q: A colleague proposes using a video diffusion model to generate physics-accurate robot training data. What's the correct pushback?
drills.a: Video diffusion optimizes for visual plausibility under the training distribution, not physical constraint satisfaction -- nothing in the DiT/flow-matching stack enforces physics. An actual simulator (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) is the correct source for physically-grounded training signal; video-gen output should be reference/pre-visualization at most.

drills.q: Staff-level: how do you decide between a full multi-step flow-matching model and an aggressively-distilled few-step consistency model for a production feature?
drills.a: Benchmark the exact step count you intend to ship at (not a more conservative one) against the full teacher on your own content distribution. High-volume, lower-stakes use cases favor the 10-100x cost cut from few-step distillation; final client-facing deliverables usually require the quality of a full or moderate-step model instead.

drills.q: What is the single biggest open problem in video generation as of August 2026, and what's the structural cause?
drills.a: Temporal consistency and physical plausibility past roughly 10-20 seconds, caused structurally by quadratic attention cost over spacetime tokens -- duration and resolution multiply their cost impact together, capping practical native generation length across the whole DiT-based industry, not just weaker vendors.
